hero.headline: Every project you have open, awake in one window
hero.sub: The desktop app stops being one window per project. Everything you have open lives in a single strip at the top, every one of them still running, and each chip tells you what its agent is doing without you going to look.

shot.alt: The desktop app with four projects open as chips across the top of one window — dreamcontext, Genevous, Tilki and kader-matematik — the last one active and showing its task board underneath, while the other three carry live session counts and unseen-activity dots
shot.caption: Four projects, one window, none of them asleep.

blocks.title: Nothing is really in the background
blocks.body: A chip is not a bookmark to a project you left. Every open project keeps running — its chat keeps streaming, its terminal keeps its scrollback — because a project going out of view is never allowed to touch its connection. The number on a chip is how many live chats that project is holding, and the dot next to it means something happened there you haven't seen yet.

shot.alt: A close crop of the chip strip: dreamcontext with a count of 1 and a magenta unseen dot, Genevous with 2 and a dot, Tilki with 6 and no dot, and kader-matematik active with a close button
shot.caption: Six live chats in Tilki, two of them unread in Genevous.

blocks.title: And it says which kind of busy

items.title: Working, not waiting
items.text: A chat mid-turn draws a green bubble with a progress ring. Before this release a project that had merely rung its bell once went magenta and stayed magenta for the whole of its next turn, so "needs you" and "getting on with it" looked identical.

items.title: Blocked gets loud
items.text: A project actually waiting on an answer bounces, the way an app bounces in the Dock, and fires a real notification even when the window is already focused — because the window being focused says nothing about which project you are looking at.

items.title: Unseen is its own mark
items.text: Something you haven't looked at yet is a separate dot rather than a colour change, so it can sit next to "working" without overwriting it.

items.title: Quiet stays quiet
items.text: A project with no live chats draws nothing at all. The strip only spends your attention when something has actually happened.

items.title: Hold ⌥, press Tab
items.text: Walk the strip while you hold Option and land when you let go — a preview you can back out of with Escape, not a jump you have to undo.

items.title: Control belongs to the terminal
items.text: The picker used to be on ⌃Tab, which sat on top of the chords a shell needs. ⌃C, ⌃D and ⌃W now reach the session you are typing in, every time.

items.title: One window is a default, not a cage
items.text: ⇧-click a project to send it to its own window anyway, for the second display.

items.title: Six stay hot
items.text: Beyond six live projects the idle ones evict to cold chips and reopen on click, so the window does not get slower the longer you work.

blocks.title: An automation now has a shape you can read
lines: derived — this manifest has no ## Flow block; this is what its
◆ run     — Step: Social Media Manager — Günlük Organik Döngü

blocks.title: …and it asks you where you already are

items.title: A ## Flow block is the manifest
items.text: Write the shape into the job and the app draws it as the job's main screen instead of a wall of prose. Don't write one and it is derived from the schedule and the prompt, as above. It describes the run; it never gets to command it.

items.title: The question lands in the chat
items.text: A run that stops for a human asks in the conversation you are already having, and its card takes over the composer while it is open — so nobody can tell a session running with bypassed permissions to "just go ahead" while the question is still unanswered.

items.title: Consent has to be consent
items.text: Trusting a changed job takes an explicit approve or reject in every channel. Free text is refused, because someone typing "no, this looks wrong" must never be read as yes.

items.title: The result reaches your phone
items.text: Connect a Telegram bot per automation and a finished run delivers its own headline, failure reason, or request for a verdict. One bot per job, so a leaked token cannot answer a different job's question.

blocks.title: The learning board reads like a board
blocks.body: Hypotheses lead with the counts that matter — open, validated, invalidated, waiting on instrumentation — and each claim carries its confidence and how long since it was last re-tested, rather than making you open it to find out.

shot.alt: The redesigned Hypotheses page: a header row counting open, validated, invalidated, awaiting-instrumentation and unread, filters for status, kind and objective, a list/board toggle, and a validated claim about hybrid recall sitting at 88% confidence
shot.caption: Last learning cycle, and how sure it is, above the fold.

items.title: Dates behave like dates
items.text: Moving a task's start reschedules its due date instead of erroring at you, finishing one stamps the day it actually ended, and a date the system writes is validated exactly like one you type.

items.title: Sleep debt can reach zero
items.text: Work that consolidation had already folded in was being booked again at the next stop, so the number could never come down all the way. It can now.

items.title: PDFs open in the app
items.text: A PDF the agent hands you opens full-window with scroll and search, and every file panel offers to open it on your computer or reveal it in Finder.

items.title: Council reports stop mid-sentence less often
items.text: A debate's sections were being cut at the first literal "z" instead of the next heading, with a broken escape underneath it. Both are fixed.

items.title: Buttons that asked you first now actually ask
items.text: In the app, every button that wanted a confirmation — deleting a task, a version or an objective, a hard sync, turning the scheduler off, removing a project from the launcher — quietly did nothing. The webview has no confirmation dialog of its own and answered “no” on your behalf, with no way to tell. They now open a real macOS sheet, and a question that cannot be shown still counts as no.

items.title: A funnel opens on its numbers
items.text: The step table on a funnel’s detail page is open by default. The lane shows the shape; the table is what you came for.

blocks.text: The desktop app is still a macOS beta and is not Apple-notarized, so a first launch may need right-click → Open. The chip strip's structure, its keyboard picking and its status marks are covered by automated runtime checks; the parts that need a real terminal and a live agent — a chat that keeps streaming across a switch, the notification that fires from a background project — were verified by hand, and are honestly still listed as such.

closer.title: Upgrade, then open a second project
closer.body: dreamcontext upgrade, then dreamcontext update in each project. Open the app, click + in the strip, and pick another vault.
